blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 164 in June to 158 in October (−3.7%), and it took 75.4% of the city’s 167 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 109 in June to 105 in October (−3.7%), and it took 41.5% of the city’s 193 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Cloverdale for detached houses in June, October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in July, August, September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in August (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, July, September, October (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Board geography differs from City geography: in the SnapStats data, "Cloverdale" is its own Fraser Valley board community — separate from the Surrey community — made up of three sub-areas: Clayton, Cloverdale and Serpentine.
Sub-area attached rows: Clayton 96 / 20 / 21%; Cloverdale 98 / 17 / 17%; Serpentine 0 / 0 / NA. Sub-area medians are not published: Not verified at sub-area level.

Town Centre plan: the City is updating the Cloverdale Town Centre Plan; the plan area is at the intersection of Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highway), and on July 22, 2024 Council expanded the plan boundary northward — bounded by 60th Avenue (south), 175 and 175A Street (west), 64 Avenue (north) and 180 Street (east), plus one lot at 18120 56 Ave, covering roughly 80.8 hectares and 145 properties. The Cloverdale Fairgrounds are a Special Study Area outside the Town Centre Plan's own scope.

Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside Cloverdale today. The City states three new stations are planned for Cloverdale under the approved expansion, and TransLink states the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain is a 16-kilometre Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029.

items.t: Form B diligence (all 7 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cloverdale

items.t: "Cloverdale" means three different geographies. The City community, the board community (Clayton + Cloverdale + Serpentine) and the Town Centre plan area are three different footprints.

Serpentine shows zero in the residential tables and still trades. Its September 2026 residential rows are 0 / 0 in both splits, yet the Cloverdale farm feed's visible listings were both Serpentine agri-business listings on 176 Street — a commercial category the residential table does not capture. A zero row is not an empty market.

Clayton was the community's fastest shelf in September 2026. Clayton's sales ratios (29% detached, 21% attached) led the Cloverdale set that month, ahead of the Cloverdale sub-area (13% / 17%) — a Clayton townhouse and a town-centre townhouse faced different shelves, on medians published only at community level.
Any automated school list built from that field alone will misfile them.

The Fairgrounds are outside the Town Centre Plan. The Cloverdale Fairgrounds — home to the Cloverdale Rodeo, held there since 1945 — are designated a Special Study Area under a separate City study and are not within the Town Centre Plan's scope, so plan-area claims for fairgrounds-adjacent property (Charlton sits near them) need the separate study, not the plan.
The Town Centre update is being built around a hospital that is not yet a fact on the ground. Price the plan as a plan, not as an operating hospital.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cloverdale
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form

Bare-land strata — the form, no Cloverdale instance verified: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure ON the lot itself: the buyer takes a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the strata's bylaws, and is entitled to a Form B Information Certificate for the lot — it is not fee-simple ownership with a road association. Tenure is read lot by lot on title.

Lot character —, no invented sizes: The research states no Cloverdale-wide lot-size table. What it states is the density machinery that governs what a lot can become: SSMUH unit counts by lot-size band, coach house / garden suite sizes of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), and the July 8, 2024 zone replacements (former RF-12 / RF-12C → R4 Small Lot Residential; RF-SD → R6 Semi-Detached).

ALR vs non-ALR split: The Cloverdale community includes ALR farm parcels on its lowland side; the ALC housing frame for those parcels is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha). Parcel-level ALR status governs; the farm ground itself is documented in
: Clayton's 9: Sun @ 72; Clayton Walk; The Grove (Clayton — a DIFFERENT complex from Walnut Grove's condo The Grove); Creekside; Ixia; The Belmont; Balmoral; The Edge; Montana.

Assemblies / development sites / proposals — documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: The Cloverdale Town Centre Plan update is a proposal in progress, not lots for sale: a plan endorsed November 18, 2019 is being updated following the October 30, 2023 endorsement of Corporate Report R176 (to support the planned new hospital and BC Cancer Centre), the boundary was expanded July 22, 2024, and the City's timeline runs to spring–summer 2027. A lot inside the plan area carries plan upside and plan uncertainty until the update is adopted.

Market context, labelled as such: SnapStats covers Cloverdale as a community but has NO land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only), and land has NO SnapStats category anywhere. Sub-area rows: Clayton detached 34 / 10 / 29%, Cloverdale detached 167 / 22 / 13%, Serpentine 0 / 0 / NA in both splits. No detached figure here is a land figure. (SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.)

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Cloverdale

items.t: Location as the City states it: Cloverdale is the third largest community in Surrey; its western border runs along 160 Street and connects with 48 Avenue, which is the southern border; Langley is to the east, and Guildford and Fleetwood are to the north, separated by 84 Avenue and 76 Avenue.

Character as the City states it: the historic centre of Surrey, settled in the mid to late 1800s, grown from a largely rural and agricultural community, named from Clover Valley, and developed along the railway into a railway and commercial hub; it has hosted the Cloverdale Rodeo at the Cloverdale Fairgrounds since 1945.

Board geography: in SnapStats, "Cloverdale" is its own Fraser Valley board community, separate from the Surrey community, made up of three sub-areas: Clayton, Cloverdale and Serpentine (September 2026, SnapStats FVR September 2026 report).
Serpentine — dual filing stated.

Town Centre plan area: at the intersection of Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highway); the boundary was expanded northward July 22, 2024 — bounded by 60th Avenue (south), 175 and 175A Street (west), 64 Avenue (north) and 180 Street (east), plus one lot at 18120 56 Ave, roughly 80.8 hectares and 145 properties.
The Cloverdale Fairgrounds are designated a Special Study Area under a separate City study and are NOT within the scope of the Cloverdale Town Centre Plan.
Search names: "Cloverdale BC," "Cloverdale Surrey," "Clayton Heights."

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Cloverdale

items.t: Zoning + the documented page defect: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs.

ALR block (applies to Cloverdale's lowland ALR parcels): ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; principal residence ≤500 m², a suite within the principal residence only, and one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha).

First-home-on-land programs — stated precisely: The FTHB GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026; 100% to $1M, maximum $50,000, phasing to $1.5M, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031) applies to new HOUSING, not bare land itself. New Housing Rebate: 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350,000–$450,000 phase-out. HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000 per year. Land-plus-build qualification: Not confirmed per transaction.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Cloverdale

items.t: City plan: The Cloverdale Town Centre Plan is being updated (boundary expanded July 22, 2024; Fairgrounds excluded as a Special Study Area).

If a strata purchase is made in Cloverdale (the townhome product here): the BC strata block applies — Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). Charlton's developer sales additionally carry 5% GST (subject to the rebates above) and the REDMA frame (disclosure statement, deposits in trust under s.18, 7-day rescission under s.21). Pad ground is not lot stock / land / acreage; pad tenancy percentages only (2026 = 2.3% + proportionate; 2027 = 2.2% + proportionate), NO pad-rent dollar figure as fact. faq.a: 3 under 280 m², 4 over 280 m², up to 6 on eligible 281 m²+ lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — subject to zone, servicing and, on ALR parcels, the ALC caps instead.
faq.q: How many units can a Cloverdale lot hold?

faq.a: In zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes, yes — 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), lane access required for a coach house on smaller R3–R6 lots, one extra parking space.
faq.q: Can I add a coach house?

faq.a: Not currently: RF-12 / RF-12C became R4 and RF-SD became R6 on July 8, 2024. Check the lot's current zone in Bylaw 12000 before quoting small-lot or coach-house potential.
faq.q: The listing says "RF-12" — is that the lot's zone?

faq.a: Compass splits by address and form: only the 18777 68A Ave townhouse units count as townhouses; the 18755 68 Ave apartment phase is condos only.
faq.q: Are Clayton Rise, Compass, Charlton, Laredo, Sunberry Court, Bacara or Manhattan Skye acreage or bare-land strata?

faq.a: On urban ground: one secondary suite per dwelling unit (at most 40% of the principal unit, never inside a coach house or garden suite), a coach house or garden suite of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² only on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), and 3–4 SSMUH units on most lots by size band, up to 6 near a frequent bus stop. On ALR ground the answer is the ALC's, not the City's: a suite only inside the principal residence, and any second dwelling is the size-capped additional residence.
faq.q: Can a Cloverdale house add a suite or a coach house?

faq.a: No. Surrey's July 8, 2024 changes replaced RF-12 / RF-12C with R4 and RF-SD with R6. Check the lot's current zone in Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 before quoting small-lot or coach-house potential.
